hints: Compare the top diagram with A, B, C and D and notice which structures disappear in each option, especially the very small ones like ribosomes, RER and small vesicles.

Remember the resolution limit of a light microscope is about $200 nm$, while an electron microscope is about $0.1 nm$, and with daylight only and no stain, only the largest, densest structure will stand out.
walkthrough:
**Observe what the electron microscope shows**

Look at the top diagram. You can see lots of tiny detail. There is a nucleus with a dark nucleolus, plus RER, Golgi body, a mitochondrion, ribosomes and small vesicles.

This is because an electron microscope has very high resolution.

**Apply the light microscope limit**

A simple light microscope has much lower resolution, about $200 nm$.

It cannot separate such tiny membranes. With daylight only and no coloured stain, small transparent organelles like mitochondria, RER and Golgi are effectively invisible.

**Pick what is still visible**

The only structure large and dense enough to absorb light and be seen unstained is the nucleus, with its darker nucleolus, plus the outline of the cell.

That matches diagram A exactly.

options.A: Correct. It shows only the cell outline, nucleus and nucleolus, which are the only structures large and dense enough to see with an unstained light microscope.
options.B: False. It still shows Golgi body, vesicles and RER fragments, which are far too small to resolve with a simple light microscope.
options.C: False. It still shows a mitochondrion with internal membranes, Golgi and vesicles, which need electron microscopy or special staining to see.
options.D: False. It shows detailed RER with ribosomes and a mitochondrion, which are only visible with the high resolution of an electron microscope.
